reason: Guest describes concrete long-side rules using daily charts, relative strength to SPY, and SMA filters that can be approximated on daily bars.

universe.description: US stocks with relative strength to SPY

setup.rule: Market (SPY) first; avoid low probability environments
setup.quote: the market comes first, right? So everything revolves around the market. 75% of all stocks... will go with SPI.

setup.rule: Stock must show relative strength to SPY
setup.quote: second is, is a stock relatively strong or relatively weak to the market?... if you look today at Google... still green... institutions are buying that stock

entry.rule: Daily chart not extended, above all SMAs, above technical indicators, near all-time high
entry.quote: I took this trade because on the daily chart, it's not extended. It's above all of its SMAs. It's above its technical indicators. It's strong, relatively strong against the market.

stop.rule: Mental stop if SPY breaks 50 SMA; no hard stops for longer holds
stop.quote: I'm looking at the SMA 50 on spy as my line... Spy needs to break that line for me to no longer want to take bullish links.

exits.rule: Hold winners; avoid quick profit taking due to skepticism
exits.quote: traders in general do not come from a rich mentality... The moment you get a dollar profit, they run away with the money

sizing.rule: Position size based on business plan for consistent monthly returns
sizing.quote: if you say, I need to make $10,000 a month, you want that to be within $8,000 to $12,000.

market_filter.rule: Only trade in direction supported by SPY trend; SPY above 50 SMA for longs
market_filter.quote: Spy needs to break that line for me to no longer want to take bullish links.

ambiguities.issue: No exact lookback, top_n or rebalance_days specified for relative strength scan
ambiguities.assumption: Use standard 20-60 session lookback and daily rebalance as implied by daily chart focus

ambiguities.issue: Mentions options and futures but core rules are for stock direction
ambiguities.assumption: Focus on long equity rules only per engine constraints
